## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

**Date:** 2026-06-08  
**Source:** [OpenAI — Introducing new capabilities to GPT-Rosalind](https://openai.com/index/introducing-new-capabilities-to-gpt-rosalind/)  
**Summary:** OpenAI announced an update to GPT-Rosalind, its life-sciences-focused model line, adding GPT-5.5-derived agentic coding, tool use, and stronger performance in drug-discovery domains including medicinal chemistry and genomics.  
**Why it matters:** OpenAI is pushing vertical frontier-model packaging into regulated enterprise R&D, where workflow integration and domain reliability matter more than generic benchmark gains.

**Date:** 2026-06-08  
**Source:** [OpenAI — Frontier models and Codex now available on AWS](https://openai.com/index/openai-frontier-models-and-codex-are-now-available-on-aws/)  
**Summary:** OpenAI said its frontier models and Codex are now available through AWS. The announcement positions GPT-5.5 and related models for enterprise use cases requiring AWS procurement, controls, and deployment paths.  
**Why it matters:** Distribution through AWS reduces enterprise adoption friction and places OpenAI models closer to existing cloud-governed workloads.

**Date:** 2026-06-08  
**Source:** [Kimi — Kimi Work](https://www.kimi.com/products/kimi-work)  
**Summary:** Moonshot/Kimi launched Kimi Work, a desktop AI agent for macOS Apple Silicon and Windows with local-file access, browser automation via WebBridge, scheduled tasks, finance-data tooling, and multi-agent workflows.  
**Why it matters:** Chinese frontier labs are moving beyond chat into OS-adjacent agent products, competing on practical workflow automation rather than model release alone.
